new.s: The Estimates Committee of Parliament took its present form in 1950 on the recommendation of:
new.x: The Estimates Committee traces to the Standing Financial Committee of 1921 but took its present form in 1950 on John Mathai's recommendation. Krishna Menon is linked to COPU (1964); Ambedkar and Mavalankar are distractors.
new.tq: Estimates = 1950, John Mathai; COPU = 1964, Krishna Menon.

new.s: The Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of the:
new.x: COPU was created in 1964 on the Krishna Menon Committee's recommendation. John Mathai is linked to the Estimates Committee (1950); Sarkaria dealt with Centre-State relations; the Rules Committee recommended DRSCs (1993).
new.tq: COPU 1964 = Krishna Menon.

new.s: The Public Accounts Committee consists of:

31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
22 members, all from the Lok Sabha
new.x: The PAC has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha (as associate members). 30 all-LS is the Estimates Committee; 31 (21+10) is a DRSC; the PAC does include Rajya Sabha members.
new.tq: PAC and COPU = 22 (15+7); Estimates = 30, all LS.

new.x: K.C. Venugopal, an Opposition member, chairs the PAC for 2026-27, in line with the convention of an Opposition chairman. Jairam Ramesh is linked to a privilege notice; Om Birla is the Speaker; Dharmendra Pradhan is the Education Minister.
new.tq: PAC chair = Opposition by convention; 2026-27 K.C. Venugopal.

o: Lok Sabha committee has 15 members nominated by the Speaker; Rajya Sabha committee has 10 members

new.tq: Privileges: LS 15 (Speaker nominates), RS 10.

new.s: Ethics Committees were constituted in the two Houses of Parliament in which order?
o: Lok Sabha in 1997, Rajya Sabha in 2000
Rajya Sabha on 4 March 1997, Lok Sabha on 16 May 2000
Both Houses on the same day in 2000
Rajya Sabha in 2000, Lok Sabha in 2004
new.x: The Rajya Sabha set up its Ethics Committee first, on 4 March 1997; the Lok Sabha followed on 16 May 2000. The other options reverse or misstate the dates.
new.tq: Ethics: RS first (1997), LS later (2000).

new.s: Which of the following committees exist only in the Lok Sabha?
o: Committee on Petitions and Committee of Privileges
Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions and Committee on Absence of Members
Rules Committee and Committee on Papers Laid on the Table
Committee on Subordinate Legislation and Committee on Government Assurances
new.x: The Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions and the Committee on Absence of Members are Lok Sabha-only. Petitions, Privileges, Rules, Papers Laid, Subordinate Legislation and Government Assurances committees exist in both Houses.
new.tq: LS-only: Private Members' Bills; Absence of Members.

new.s: Which parliamentary committee is described as a 'continuous economy committee'?
new.x: The Estimates Committee is called a 'continuous economy committee' because it suggests economies and alternative policies. The PAC is the 'watchdog' on expenditure; the Petitions Committee is the 'Ombudsman'; the Business Advisory Committee allots time.
new.tq: Estimates = economy; PAC = watchdog; Petitions = Ombudsman.

new.s: In Raja Ram Pal (2007), the Supreme Court held that decisions of a House in matters of privilege are:
o: Reviewable only for gross illegality or unconstitutionality
Reviewable on every ground of procedural irregularity
Subject to approval by the President
new.x: Raja Ram Pal (2007) held that privilege decisions can be reviewed, but only for gross illegality or unconstitutionality. They are not wholly immune; mere procedural irregularity is protected by Art. 122/212; the President has no approving role.
new.tq: Raja Ram Pal 2007 = limited review of privilege decisions.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Monsoon Session of 2026:
1. Question Hour ran for only 1% of its scheduled time in the Lok Sabha and 12% in the Rajya Sabha.
2. The estimated loss from disruptions was about Rs 175 crore.
3. All 12 Bills passed were debated in detail.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Question Hour ran 1% (LS) and 12% (RS) of scheduled time, and the estimated loss was Rs 175 crore. Statement 3 is wrong: of the 12 Bills passed, only one (the Public Examination Amendment Bill) was debated in detail. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
new.tq: Monsoon 2026: QH 1%/12%, Rs 175 crore, 12 Bills, one debated.

new.s:
Assertion (A): India has a parliamentary form of government.
Reason (R): In India the executive is responsible to the legislature.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
new.x: Both are true and R explains A: responsibility of the executive (the Council of Ministers) to the legislature is the defining test of the parliamentary system. So options 2, 3 and 4 are wrong.
new.tq: Parliamentary = executive responsible to legislature (UPPSC 2025).

new.s: The oath of office to the Governor of a State is administered by:
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court of the State, or in his absence the senior-most judge
The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
new.x: Under Article 159, the Chief Justice of the High Court (or, in his absence, the senior-most judge available) administers the Governor's oath. The President appoints but does not swear in the Governor; the CJI and the Speaker have no role.
new.tq: Governor's oath = Chief Justice of the HC (Art. 159).

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act enabled the appointment of the same person as Governor of two or more States?
new.x: The 7th Amendment Act, 1956 allowed one person to be Governor of two or more States. The 1st, 42nd and 44th Amendments deal with other matters.
new.tq: Common Governor = 7th Amendment, 1956.

new.s: When a Governor is appointed administrator of an adjoining Union Territory under Article 239(2), he acts:
o: On the aid and advice of his own State Council of Ministers
Independently of his own State Council of Ministers
Only on the advice of the State Legislature
Only with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court
new.x: Under Article 239(2), the Governor administering an adjoining UT acts independently of his State's Council of Ministers; it is an express discretion. He is not bound by State ministers, the legislature or the High Court in this role.
new.tq: Art. 239(2) = express discretion, independent of State ministry.

new.s: Who was the first Governor of Andhra State (1953) and of Andhra Pradesh (1956)?
new.x: C.M. Trivedi was the first Governor of both Andhra State (1953) and Andhra Pradesh (1956). E.S.L. Narasimhan was the common Governor of AP and Telangana (2014-19); Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was the first CM and K.V. Ranga Reddy the Deputy CM of united AP.
new.tq: First AP Governor = C.M. Trivedi.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Chief Minister in Andhra Pradesh:
1. K. Pawan Kalyan of the Jana Sena is Deputy CM in 2026.
2. The 2019-24 government had five Deputy CMs.
3. The office is expressly created by Article 164.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Pawan Kalyan (Jana Sena) is Deputy CM, and the 2019-24 government had five Deputy CMs. Statement 3 is wrong: Deputy CM is not a constitutional post. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
new.tq: Deputy CM = political post; AP had five in 2019-24.

facts.f: Does not appoint HC judges; cannot remove SPSC members

new.s: Which one of the following can the Governor of a State NOT do?
o: Appoint the Chairman of the State Public Service Commission
Remove a member of the State Public Service Commission
new.x: Although the Governor appoints SPSC members, only the President can remove them. The Governor does appoint the Advocate-General (Art. 165), the SPSC Chairman (Art. 316) and the State Election Commissioner (Art. 243K).
new.tq: Governor appoints SPSC, but only the President removes.

facts.f: West Bengal: Mamata refused to resign; Art 164 pleasure

new.s: In May 2026, after Mamata Banerjee refused to resign despite losing the election, which provision was cited as allowing the Governor to dismiss a Chief Minister who has lost majority?
new.x: Ministers hold office during the Governor's pleasure under Article 164, which allows dismissal of a CM who has lost majority. Article 356 is President's Rule, Article 163(3) bars inquiry into ministerial advice, and Article 361 grants the Governor immunity.
new.tq: CM who lost majority → Art. 164 pleasure.

new.s: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Chief Minister of a State appointed by the Governor?
new.x: Article 164(1) provides that the Governor appoints the Chief Minister. Article 163(1) concerns aid and advice, Article 167 the CM's duties towards the Governor, and Article 174 sessions of the legislature.
new.tq: CM appointment = Art. 164(1) (APPSC-GS 2021).

new.s: Under Article 164(2), the State Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the:
o: Both Houses of the State Legislature
new.x: Article 164(2) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly alone. Ministers hold office at the Governor's pleasure but are not collectively responsible to him; the Council is not responsible to the Legislative Council.
new.tq: Collective responsibility = Legislative Assembly (BPSC 2022).

new.s: Who was the first woman Chief Minister of an Indian State?
new.x: Sucheta Kripalani became CM of Uttar Pradesh in 1963, the first woman CM. Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor (UP, 1947); Nandini Satpathy became Odisha CM later; Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was never a CM.
new.tq: First woman CM = Sucheta Kripalani; first woman Governor = Sarojini Naidu.

new.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh (1956)?
new.x: Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was the first CM of united Andhra Pradesh (1956-60). Tanguturi Prakasam was CM of Andhra State, Burgula Ramakrishna Rao of Hyderabad State, and N. Chandrababu Naidu the first CM of residuary AP (2014).
new.tq: United AP 1956 = Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy; residuary AP 2014 = Naidu.
